7900.full: a loosening by the side: paralysis, palsy , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

7902.full: a falling beside; κατὰ τὴν π. τινος in the course of an action, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

s: in cl., marked amiss, spurious, counterfeit. Later
marked with a sign ; as subst., a figure­head
7904.full: παράσημος, -ον (σῆμα, a mark) [in LXX: 3Ma.2:29 * ;] __1. in cl., marked amiss, spurious, counterfeit. Later, __2. marked at the side, annotated (Plut.). __3. marked with a sign (LXX); as subst., a figure­head : Act.28:11 (see MM, xix).† (AS)

7905.full: 1. a putting aside or away, banishing, relegatio , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. a setting out things for sale, retail-trade , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. παρίσταμαι); intransitive a being beside : 4. a position or post near a king, (Xenophon Historicus) 5. presence of mind, courage , (Polybius Historicus): also, desperation , (Polybius Historicus) 6. as law-term, a small money deposit on entering law-suits, (Isaeus Orator) (ML)

7911.full: πεζός, -ή, -όν (πούς), [in LXX for רַגְלִי ;] __1. on foot: Mat.14:13 (WH, mg., R, txt.). __2. Opp. to going by sea, by land: Mat.14:13 (WH, mg., R, mg.). __3. As adv., πεζῇ (sc. ὁδῷ), on foot or by land: Mt 1413 (WH, txt.), Mrk.6:33.† (AS)

7913.full: to hew or shape with an axe , Lat. dolare, (Odyssey by Homer) (in epic aor1 πελέκκησε), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

7924.full: πεποίθησις, -εως, ἡ (πείθω), [in LXX: 4Ki.18:19 (בִּטָּחוֹן)* ;] confidence: 2Co.1:15 3:4 10:2, Eph.3:12; before εἰς, 2Co.8:22; ἐν, Php.3:4 (the word is condemned by the Atticists, see Rutherford, NPhr., 355).† (AS)

7928.g: to tie the hands behind the back
7928.full: tie the hands behind the back

7930.full: περι-αστράπτω [in LXX: 4Ma.4:10 * ;] to flash around: with accusative, Act.9:3; before περί Act.22:6 (Eccl, and Byzant.).† (AS)

7932.full: 1. poetry περί-βωτος, noised abroad, much talked of, famous , (Thucydides) 2. in bad sense, notorious, scandalous , (Demosthenes Orator):—;adverb -τως, notoriously , (Aeschines Orator) 3. with or amid shouts , epithet of Ares, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

7938.full: περι-δέω [in LXX: Job.12:18 (אָסַר)* ;] to tie round, bind round: with accusative and dative, pass., Jhn.11:44.† (AS)

s: to waste one's labour about a thing
7940.full: περι-εργάζομαι [in LXX: Wis.8:5 א1, Sir.3:23 * ;] __1. to waste one's labour about a thing. __2. to be a busybody: 2Th.3:11 (cf. Plat., Apol., 19 B).† (AS)

7943.full: to burn round about: —; Pass. to be all scorched , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

7947.full: περι-κάθαρμα, -τος, τό (περικαθαίρω, to purify on all sides or completely, Deu.18:10, Jos.5:4, 4Ma.1:29*), [in LXX: Pro.21:18 (כֹּפֶר)* ;] __1. a victim, expiation (Pr, l.with). __2. refuse, rubbish: pl., 1Co.4:13 (see ICC, in l).† (AS)

7953.full: edged with purple , π. ἐσθής a robe with a purple border , the Roman toga praetextata or laticlavia , (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

s: to slip away on all sides
7954.full: 1. with accusative to flow round , τὸν δ᾽ αἷμα περίρρεε (Odyssey by Homer); νῆσον π. ὁ Νεῖλος (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be surrounded by water , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to slip away on all sides , ἡ ἀσπὶς περιερρύη εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν slipped off his arm into the sea, (Thucydides); [ αἱ πέδαι] αὐτόμαται π. (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to overflow on all sides , σοὶ περιρρείτω βίος may thy means of living abound , (Sophocles Tragicus); οὐδενὸς περιρρέοντος being superfluous , (Plutarch):—;Pass. to be all dripping , ἱδρῶτι with sweat, (Plutarch) (ML)

s: to break or tear off all around
7955.full: περι-ρήγνυμι (Rec. -ρρ-, see supr.) [in LXX: 2Ma.4:38 * ;] to break or tear off all around: frequently of garments, τ. ἰμάτια, Act.16:22.† (AS)

7961.full: περι-τρέπω [in LXX: Wis.5:23 * ;] to turn about, turn: with accusative and, dative, Act.26:24 (cf. FlJ, Ant., ix, 4, 4).† (AS)

7966.full: looked at from all sides, admired of all observers , (Euripides) (ML)

s: a way round, the circumference, circuit, compass
a going round in a circle, circuit
7969.full: 1. a going round, a flank march , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a way round, the circumference, circuit, compass , τοῦ τείχεος, τῆς λίμνης (Herdotus Historicus); absolute, τὴν π. in circumference , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. γῆς π. a chart or map of the earth (compare πίναξ); (Herdotus Historicus) 4. a going round in a circle, circuit , (Plutarch) 5. of Time, a cycle or period of time , (Pindar), etc. 6. a prescribed course of life, system , (Plato Philosophus) 7. a fit of intermittent fever, (Demosthenes Orator) 8. = περιφορά, a course at dinner , (Xenophon Historicus); π. λόγων table-talk , (Xenophon Historicus) 9. the orbit of a heavenly body , (Xenophon Historicus) 10. a well-rounded sentence, period , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

s: that which is over and above, superfluity, abundance
7970.full: περίσσευμα, -τος, τό (περισσεύω) [in LXX: Ecc.2:15 * ;] that which is over and above, superfluity, abundance: opposite to ὑστέρημα (which see), 2Co.8:13-14; pl., Mrk.8:8; metaphorically, π. τ. καρδίας, Mat.12:34, Luk.6:45 (cf. Ec, l.with; Plut., al.).† (AS)

7971.full: 1. very thoughtful, very careful, notable , of Penelope, (Homer) 2. like ὑπέρφρων, haughty, over-weening , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. with genitive despising a thing, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

s: that which is wiped off, offscouring
7972.full: περί-ψημα, -τος, τό (περιψράω, to wipe off all round), [in LXX: Tob.5:18 * ;] that which is wiped off, offscouring: metaphorically (assoc. with περικάθαρμα, which see), 1Co.4:13 (and so prob., To, l.with, as EV; but see Thayer, see word, for the meaning expiation, ransom, in To; and cf. LS, see word κάθαρμα; Lft., Notes, 200 f., and on Ign., Eph., 8).† (AS)

7976.full: disable, cripple (JHN.12:40 - variant א P66 P75)

7978.full: πιέζω [in LXX : Mic.6:15 (דָּרַךְ)* ;] __1. to press, press down or to­gether: Luk.6:38 (cl). __2. Later, to seize (see: πιάζω).† (AS)

7979.full: πλανήτης, -ου, ὁ (πλανάω), [in LXX: Hos.9:17 (נָדַד) * ;] = πλάνης, a wanderer: ἀστέρες π. (cl. planets), wandering stars, Ju 13 (WH, mg., -τες).† (AS)

7980.full: mostly, most often, very often , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

7984.full: fulness, a throng, a crowd , of people, (Homer), etc. (ML)

s: to bring in full measure, hence, to fulfil, accomplish
to persuade, assure or satisfy fully
7986.full: πληροφορέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ecc.8:11 (מָלֵא) * ;] __1. to bring in full measure, hence, to fulfil, accomplish: Luk.1:1, 2Ti.4:5 4:17. __2. to persuade, assure or satisfy fully (so in π.; see Deiss., LAE, 82 f.; M, Th., 9): pass., Rom.4:21 14:5, Col.4:12 (see Lft., in l). __3. to fill: Rom.15:13, L, mg. (Cl. Ro., 1Co.5:4); metaphorically, pass., to be filled with, hence, fully bent on (Ec, l.with).† (AS)

s: to make in the form of a plinth
7988.full: 1. to make into bricks , τὴν γῆν (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to make bricks , (Aristophanes Comicus);—;so in Mid., thuc. 2. to build of brick , τείχη (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to make in the form of a plinth or brick , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

7990.full: 1. a twining: anything woven, a web , (Euripides) 2. metaphorically the complication of a plot, opposite to λύσις, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

7992.full: πλήμμυρα, -ης (for Att.. -ας, see Bl., § 7, 1) (πλήθω), [in LXX: π. γένεσθαι, Job.40:18 (23) (נָהָר עָשַׁק) * ;] a flood (of sea or river) : Luk.6:48.† (AS)

7994.full: πλόος, πλούς genitive, -όου, -oῦ (and in late writers also πλοός, like νοός from νοῦς), ὁ (πλέω), [in LXX: Wis.14:1 * ;] a voyage: Act.21:7 27:9-10.† (AS)
